escalations.description: Problems page 1, Фиг. 2а: the baseline of the body-text line „е P = 12 W.“ and the top of the lamp circle share the same row (1495 px at 160 dpi). The gold box top is set to 799‰ on that row; on the pipeline's 300-dpi crop check that no hairline of the text shows and that the lamp circle's top is intact – move the top to 800‰ if a text sliver appears.

All 29 candidate crop files listed in the task were missing on disk (figs/ directory empty); every figure judgment here was made on crops rendered locally from the 160-dpi page PNGs with the same permille formula. When the pipeline re-cuts the 13 gold boxes at 300 dpi, a human should glance at them once (especially the four solution figures, whose captions are included on purpose).

summary: The gold was built from the sonnet candidate, whose text is the only one that is verbatim (haiku and glm each change words and silently fix source errors), but its problem statements duplicate the parts and its figure boxes clip the P labels on Фиг. 1а/1б, swallow a text line on Фиг. 2а and cut the lens bottoms on the four solution figures; all thirteen boxes were re-measured from the pages. Haiku's nine boxes all land on body text and it omits the solution figures entirely; glm groups figures, swallows body text and misses Фиг. 3в altogether. Of the checkers, the glm-for-haiku run is 9/9 true (though its one figure finding misdescribes a critical box as minor), the glm-for-sonnet run is 2/4 (one invented spelling, one false blanket pass on the crops), and the haiku-for-glm run returned no findings and a wrong 'pass' verdict despite five critical figure boxes.
